author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader browses the clinic's specialties and the veterinarians holding each
summary: A specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, and under each the veterinarians holding it by full name. All specialties render on one page; a veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear.
acceptance_criteria: Every specialty the clinic knows is listed under the name it is stored as.
Each veterinarian holding a specialty is shown under it by first name followed by last name.
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page.
All specialties appear on the single page, with no page-at-a-time control.
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, showing no veterinarian under it.
The specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order.
A veterinarian holding more than one specialty appears under each of them.
non_goals: Adding, renaming, or removing a specialty or a veterinarian from this page (NG-2 unchanged)
Paging, sorting controls, or filtering of the specialty list
Searching for a specialty or a veterinarian (NG-9)
Adding the page to the site navigation - left as an open question in docs/prd.md
notes: Read-only view of the existing directory; the product owner confirmed NG-2 stays unchanged. REQ-LANG-002 binds the new page's wording: no hard-coded user-facing text, and every new message present in all eleven bundles. Ordering (edge case 2) and the unheld-specialty case (edge case 1) were not stated by the product owner; both are resolved here for testability, consistent with REQ-VET-001 edge case 1, and are cheap to revise.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is the vet feature package's existing shape applied to a second read-only page: a Spring Data repository, a package-private @Controller, and a Thymeleaf template under templates/vets/. One adjustment carries the slice. An unheld specialty is unreachable through VetRepository, because the veterinarian-specialty association is mapped on Vet alone (system-design.md#contracts, 'Invariants the rows cannot carry'), so the slice adds SpecialtyRepository for the specialty side and derives the inverse grouping in memory from VetRepository.findAll(). Do not add a bidirectional @ManyToMany(mappedBy) to Specialty: it would change an eagerly-fetched entity graph and risk a cycle in the Vets serialization wrapper that the /vets route returns. The grouping is assembled by an immutable SpecialtyDirectory value object (architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog, 'Value object'), not in the controller, so the controller stays bind-delegate-select and the ordering and omission rules are unit-testable without Spring. No new pattern, module, package, or dependency.
integration_points: Route GET /specialties.html, given by the product owner and absent from the PRD by design; served by a new package-private SpecialtyController in the vet package, returning view name vets/specialtyList. Weighed against a third @GetMapping on VetController and rejected: VetController's second route (/vets) is a Known Defect pending removal, and the Web controller pattern row is one HTTP surface per controller.

SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> (the narrow base VetRepository uses, not JpaRepository) with a single read method carrying an explicit @Query ... ORDER BY name, mirroring PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes(). Store-side ordering satisfies the stable-order edge case for specialties.
The veterinarian side reuses the existing cached VetRepository.findAll(); no new query and no new cache.
The template extends fragments/layout with the menu argument 'vets' so the veterinarians nav item reads as active. No nav entry is added - that is a declared non-goal and an open PRD question.
Two @MockitoBean repositories in the @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class) slice; the SpecialtyDirectory unit test uses real Vet and Specialty instances per the mocking policy.

patterns.description: lookup-table repository returning rows in name order via an explicit @Query - the model for SpecialtyRepository
narrow Repository base with only the methods actually called - minimal surface, and the cached findAll() the directory reuses
veterinarian full name rendered as firstName + ' ' + lastName - reuse verbatim; the new page renders the same composition
package-private @Controller holding a repository by constructor injection and returning a view name

risks.risk: Copying @Cacheable("vets") onto the new repository method. CacheConfiguration creates only the 'vets' JCache cache, so a second name would not exist, and a second cache with no eviction extends open question 5 on vet cache invalidation.
risks.mitigation: Leave SpecialtyRepository uncached. The specialty list is three rows in seed data; the veterinarian side already reads through the cached VetRepository.findAll().

risks.risk: Copying the pagination block out of vetList.html. Any page-at-a-time control fails the acceptance criterion directly.
risks.mitigation: The handler takes no @RequestParam and no Pageable, and the template carries no pagination block. Assert the whole specialty set on the single response.

risks.risk: Hard-coded user-facing text on the new page fails REQ-LANG-002 and I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkNonInternationalizedStrings, which walks src/main and flags any HTML text node lacking a th:text attribute.
risks.mitigation: Every text node carries th:text. The keys this page needs - specialties, vets, name, none - all exist in all eleven bundles already, so the page can ship with no new key. Any genuinely new key goes into all eleven.

risks.risk: XSS through rendered specialty or veterinarian names.
risks.mitigation: Render with th:text only, never th:utext; Thymeleaf escapes expression output by default and the application does not disable it. This matches the mitigation already recorded in the threat model.

risks.risk: SpecialtyDirectory is not framework-instantiated, so the scoped persistence-entity exception in architecture-principles.md does not cover it.
risks.mitigation: It must realize the closed Domain Core properties in full: immutable, defensive copies of the collections it is handed, null inputs rejected at construction, no repository or Spring type referenced.

notes: Route GET /specialties.html is a product-owner-stated constraint carried outside the PRD, not a design choice; routes are mechanism and belong in system-design.md#contracts. Ordering: specialties by name from the store; veterinarians under each by last name then first name, decided here to make the stable-order edge case testable and cheap to revise. The three remaining edge cases fall out of the derivation rather than needing separate handling - an unheld specialty yields an entry with an empty veterinarian list, a veterinarian holding nothing enters no entry, and a veterinarian holding several appears under each. Trust boundary: one unauthenticated HTTP GET with no request parameter and no body, so nothing crosses inward to validate; the boundary control is that the handler is read-only and its output is escaped. The page publishes no data /vets.html does not already publish, so the security posture is unchanged. The prd-entry named VetController.java, VetRepository.java and VetControllerTests.java as file targets; this design puts the work in new sibling files in the same package instead, and touches none of those three. docs/system-design.md gained one current-state sentence under Contracts recording the one-directional association; the Contracts rows for the new types are left to doc-sync after implementation, so the table keeps describing code that exists. Follow-up for the PRD owner, not blocking: 'specialty directory' is now a PRD term with no entry in docs/ubiquitous-language.md. Process lapse to note: the dispatch-start record at line 3 was appended mid-dispatch rather than as the first tool call.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Template output escaping verified, not assumed: every text node in src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html uses th:text (auto-escaped). A literal sweep of the new template and the layout fragment it replaces into found no th:utext, no [(...)] unescaped inline, no th:inline='javascript', and no th:attr/th:href sink carrying directory data. The one SpEL concatenation, ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName + ' '}, is a fixed template-authored expression over entity fields; its rendered result is escaped like any other th:text value, so stored XSS through a veterinarian or specialty name is not reachable here.

JPQL is injection-free: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a static @Query string ('SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name') with no parameters, no bind variables and no string concatenation. The ORDER BY column is literal, so the usual JPQL dynamic-sort injection shape is absent. VetRepository.findAll() is a derived query. No native SQL, no EntityManager.createQuery over a built string.

No-user-input claim verified against the code: @GetMapping('/specialties.html') declares no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @RequestBody, @ModelAttribute or Principal argument; the only parameter is Model. The handler returns the constant VIEW_SPECIALTY_LIST, so no request-derived value reaches the view-name resolver and Thymeleaf template injection through a dynamic fragment/view expression is not possible.

Read-only and mutation-free: SpecialtyRepository extends the marker Repository (not CrudRepository/JpaRepository), so no save/delete method is exposed at all, and its single method is @Transactional(readOnly = true). SpecialtyDirectory is a record whose canonical constructors defensively List.copyOf both entries and Entry.veterinarians, and SpecialtyDirectoryTests asserts the exposed lists are unmodifiable — no aliasing of repository-owned collections into the model.

No secrets introduced: swept the full diff for credential-shaped names (token, password, secret, key, credential, passwd, api) — the only 'key' hits are HashMap keys in the in-memory grouping. No connection strings, no configuration or property file touched, and no logging of any kind added, so no PII or operational data reaches a log sink.

Supply chain unchanged: scripts/changeset.sh --name-only shows build.gradle, settings.gradle and gradle/ are untouched, so no dependency, version or repository coordinate is added or moved and there is no new CVE surface from this slice. No dependencyCheck plugin is configured in build.gradle, so dependencyCheckAnalyze is not an available task on this project.

Exposure delta is bounded and consistent with the documented posture: the new route publishes specialty names plus veterinarian first/last names — the same clinic-internal data already served unauthenticated by /vets.html — minus veterinarians holding no specialty. The only genuinely new datum is the existence of a specialty no veterinarian holds. The project-wide absence of authentication, authorization and CSRF is a pre-existing condition already recorded in docs/system-design.md Security Context and its Threat Model; this read-only GET adds no state change, so it does not widen that surface and is not raised as a new finding.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Edge case 1 from prd.md ('A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, showing no veterinarian under it') and the template's #{none} span with th:if="${#lists.isEmpty(entry.veterinarians)}" (specialtyList.html:20-21) are covered only at the SpecialtyDirectory unit level (100% branch coverage there). No test boots the templating engine with an unheld specialty: the controller-test fixture gives every one of the three specialties (dentistry, radiology, surgery) a holder, so the 'none' message-key resolution and the th:if branch in the real template are never exercised end to end. A wrong key, a broken th:if condition, or a malformed fragment in that branch would pass every current test.
findings.fix: Add a fourth specialty with no holding vet to the @BeforeEach fixture (e.g. specialty(4, "oncology")), and add an assertion (or extend theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByStoredName) that the rendered page contains "oncology" and the resolved #{none} text for that row, distinguishing it from any vet name.

findings.description: Derived Expectations (testing-principles.md) requires expected values to be a function of the test's inputs. theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowHoldingVeterinariansByFullName and theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty assert against the literal strings "Helen Leary", "Linda Douglas", and "James Carter" rather than deriving them from the leary()/douglas()/carter() fixture methods that construct those same vets two lines above in setup(). A rename in the fixture (e.g. changing carter()'s last name) would silently desynchronize the literal and the assertion instead of failing loudly.
findings.fix: Build the expected full-name strings from the fixture methods, e.g. leary().getFirstName() + " " + leary().getLastName(), or expose the vet objects to the assertions so the expected string is computed rather than duplicated as a literal.

findings.description: Testing Vocabulary (testing-principles.md: 'Extract shared test utilities into a common base class or utility module') is violated by near-identical private specialty(id, name) and vetHolding(firstName, lastName, Specialty...) factories duplicated across both new test classes in the same package. Both are new files under the naming-school cutoff, so this is new duplication, not inherited debt.
findings.fix: Extract specialty(...) and vetHolding(...) into a shared package-visible test fixture helper (e.g. a VetFixtures utility class or a common test base) that both SpecialtyDirectoryTests and SpecialtyControllerTests use.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectoryTests uses only real Vet/Specialty instances per the brief's mocking policy — no mocks on the domain value object
SpecialtyControllerTests keeps mocking to the two repository boundaries via @MockitoBean under @WebMvcTest, the brief's sanctioned web-boundary exception

Grouping/ordering/omission logic sits in the framework-free SpecialtyDirectory unit tests (100% line and branch coverage per jacocoTestReport), correctly applying the pyramid's 'could this be tested without booting the framework' test
All PRD acceptance criteria and edge cases 1-3 have a dedicated test at the unit level: unheld specialty, stable order, multi-specialty vet

AssertJ used fluently in SpecialtyDirectoryTests (extracting/satisfies/containsExactly); MockMvc's content().string(containsString(...)) in the controller test is the standard idiom for the sanctioned MockMvc boundary
Immutability (null-rejection, unmodifiable collections) is explicitly tested on the value object
Four-phase structure with blank-line separation observed throughout, no phase comments or narration
Test names follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school required for tests written after 2026-07-31
./gradlew test and jacocoTestReport both green; no flaky or order-dependent tests observed
